insight.title: What the world is made of when nobody is looking
insight.subtitle: The elegant architecture of the space between us.

sections.text: Look at the palms of your hands. They feel solid, heavy, and permanent. Yet, nature hides a quiet secret about the fabric of our world. Almost everything you see is made of nothing at all. If we removed the empty space from every human, our entire species would fit inside a single sugar cube.

The atoms that build your body are like miniature, silent solar systems. Each one is a vast cathedral with a tiny center. They only feel solid because invisible fields push back against your fingers. You never truly touch a lover’s hand; you simply hover near it, held apart by a microscopic, electric push.

This hidden architecture changes how we view the mundane. We are not heavy sculptures of clay, but light, intricate clouds of energy. It is a beautiful irony that the things we find most substantial are mostly made of ghosts. In a vast emptiness, the simple act of holding on is the greatest miracle of all.

news.title: 'Serendipitous' discovery of Martian ripple marks reveals an ancient sandstorm
news.description: The search for life on Mars involves the efforts of scientists from many different disciplines. An important aspect of that search is to study Martian sedimentary rocks for information about the planet's environment when it is likely that the surface environment hosted abundant water and therefore more habitable, around three to four billion years ago. Now, research published in the journal Geology shows evidence of an intense sandstorm that swept through Mars's Gale crater over three billion years ago.

news.title: Mesoporous silica catalyst enables α-allylation of simple ketones using allyl alcohols
news.description: A research team reports they have created an organic reaction called α-allylation with simple ketones and allyl alcohols. This work holds the potential for use in the development of next-generation catalysts. The research is published in the journal ACS Catalysis on March 2, 2026.

news.title: CDC pauses lab testing of rabies, monkeypox and other diseases
news.description: The federal government’s disease-tracking agency has paused its diagnostic testing for rabies, monkeypox and a number of other infectious diseases.
